title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String
corePattern: String Matching - Sliding Window Comparison vs Prefix Automaton (KMP) vs Rolling Hash
interviewTips: Clarify edge cases: what if needle is empty, needle longer than haystack, or both length 1? Confirm return 0 vs -1 conventions.

Trade-off to discuss: Brute Force O(n*m) with O(1) space is simplest and passes small constraints, KMP gives guaranteed O(n+m) with O(m) space, Rabin-Karp gives average O(n+m) but needs hash collision handling.
Edge-case tip: highly repetitive inputs like haystack=aaaaa...aab and needle=aaaab expose worst-case brute force; explain how LPS fallback avoids re-scanning.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Sliding Window
approaches.intuition: Try every possible start position i in haystack and check if needle matches character by character. First match wins, otherwise continue. This is first-principles string matching.
approaches.theory: For n=len(haystack), m=len(needle), there are n-m+1 alignments. For each alignment i, compare haystack[i+j] vs needle[j] for j in 0..m-1. Break on first mismatch. If all m match, return i. If no alignment matches, return -1. Correct because we exhaustively check all valid starting indices in order.

timeComplexity.explanation: Up to n-m+1 alignments, each compares up to m chars. Worst case e.g. haystack=aaaaa...a, needle=aaaab causes almost m compares per alignment.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only indices i and j are used, no extra arrays. Slicing version would be O(m) for substring copy.

steps: i=0: compare s-a-d vs s-a-d -> all match, return 0

edgeCases: repetitive prefix causing many partial matches

approaches.name: Approach 2: Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP)
approaches.intuition: When a mismatch happens, we already know the matched prefix of needle. Use its longest proper prefix which is also suffix (LPS) to skip ahead without moving haystack pointer backwards.
approaches.theory: Precompute LPS array where lps[i] = length of longest proper prefix of needle[0..i] that is also suffix. During scan, maintain j = length of current matched prefix of needle. On match haystack[i]==needle[j], advance both. On mismatch, fallback j=lps[j-1] instead of restarting from 0, preserving the overlapping prefix. This simulates a prefix automaton and each character is processed at most twice, giving linear time.

timeComplexity.explanation: O(m) to build LPS and O(n) to scan haystack. Each step either advances i or reduces j, so total fallback steps are amortized linear.

spaceComplexity.explanation: LPS array of size m stores prefix function for needle.

steps: Scan: match aabaa, mismatch at haystack[5]=a vs needle[5]=f, fallback j=lps[4]=2
Continue without rewinding i, eventually match at index 3

edgeCases: needle='aaaab' with haystack='aaaaa...aaaab' -> KMP stays linear while brute force is quadratic
needle with no self-overlap e.g. 'abcdef' -> lps all zero
needle length 1 -> lps=[0], reduces to linear scan

approaches.name: Approach 3: Rabin-Karp Rolling Hash
approaches.intuition: Compare hash values of needle and each length-m window of haystack instead of comparing all characters. Slide window in O(1) by removing left char and adding right char.
approaches.theory: Use polynomial hash H = c0*B^(m-1)+...+c(m-1) mod MOD. Precompute power=B^(m-1) mod MOD, needleHash and first windowHash in O(m). Roll: windowHash = ((windowHash - haystack[i]*power)*B + haystack[i+m]) mod MOD. If hashes equal, verify with direct O(m) compare to rule out collision. Average linear because hash mismatch filters most windows; worst case still O(n*m) if many collisions or adversarial input.

timeComplexity.complexity: O(n + m) average, O(n * m) worst
timeComplexity.explanation: O(m) to hash needle and first window, O(n) rolling steps O(1) each. Direct verification only on hash hit, so average linear; worst case with many hits degrades to brute force.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only a few hash variables and power value, no array proportional to input.

steps: window 0 he: hash mismatch, roll to el
window 1 el: mismatch, roll to ll
window 2 ll: hash match + verify true, return 2

edgeCases: hash collision requires explicit substring verify
large m needs mod to avoid overflow, use long long
single char needle -> power=1 loop skipped
